title: Booking agents and crooks
summary: Bands dealt with individual bookers, not agencies: Bernard Galway, Al Travis and Chauncey Holland were crooks, Joe Glazer wanted him to hold out for big money, and Mo Gale asked for a sliding commission up to 35%.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: I've got so many things I want to ask you about and I hate to skip about, but tell me about booking syndicates in Texas and Oklahoma and Arizona and different places like that.
Yeah, you would deal with individuals, wasn't any big agencies.
Yeah, you would deal with one man?

One man. How much territory? The man that first picked me up was Bernard Galway. And I had him, not only was his name, but Rabinowitz. And then finally this Al Travis that was the biggest crook in the world. And then the next biggest crook was this one that I picked up here, Chauncey Highland, on the revision of my band. Those were crooks. They weren't under bondage like the big companies are now. And the only major company that I went with that was under bonds was when I went to Joe Glazer. See, Glazer wanted me to hold out for big money. And my band could wait for 40, 50 bucks a night. And he didn't want it. He wanted me to stay out for big money. So consequently, I had to come back where I could make a living with the band. And Ella Fitzgerald had Mo Gale to meet me up at the Safari Ballroom. And we all met up there and Mo Gale. In those days I was such a young man, I didn't have anyone to advise me. And I always thought that I had got stung a couple of times when Mo Gale asked me to surrender 35% of my earnings after it got to a certain amount of money. Which, if I had accepted it, I would be making far more money than just saying, well, no, I'm not going to give you 35%. Because it started at 10%, say for $150 a night, and 200 you would get 15% and modulated up to where it got to 35%. But when it got to 35%, it was in the thousands.
And then I could have stayed with Gale's office, but no.
